findings.title: Reject a later mobile bind that reuses any issued structure identity
findings.mechanism: New structure issuance rejects IDs already held by current/retired roster entries, but campaign_roster_link_member only checks find_duplicate_host_id against roster records before committing a later bind. A host can issue structureX first and later return sameX for a new mobile. Both registries accept it; resolve_report_target checks structure records before roster, so report_object(X) intended for the mobile damages/kills the structure. If structureX was retired, its retained record shadows the new mobile and refuses the report as ended. The ever-issued/no-reuse invariant must hold in both directions.
findings.bounded_correction: Expose a private ever-issued structure-ID query/shared namespace check and invoke it before committing a roster bind, including retired IDs. Preserve mobile default numbering/RNG, opaque IDs and independent host authority; no namespace parsing or pointer/index leakage. Add both-order live/retired/same-slot controls exercising real binding/registry integration before record commit; existing object_checks uses fixed roster stub and cannot detect this reverse bind defect.

findings.title: Carry registered persistent identities in actual physical-subject requests
findings.mechanism: New persistent IDs are wired into blast/bridgevehicle windows and inbound reports, but common source/target fill_host_id still consults only roster, so even a registered structure has no ID in that envelope. Real DAMAGE/HEALTH/IMPACT helpers zero the envelope and copy only by-value figures; calls with an actual subject do not convey its available persistent identity. Host state/report correlation is therefore window-only plus inboundAPI, not all physical subjects. Stateless numeric solvers can remain valid, but this does not fulfill the broader R3 persistent-correlation responsibility by itself.

findings.title: Document the actual borrowed lifetime of structure identity strings
findings.mechanism: New header promises strings live for the engine session, but IDs are inline in the reallocatable records array.
